# keepsake: shared memory for fleets of agents

Keepsake gives agents a durable, shared knowledge base they read and write over
MCP. It runs on Kubernetes or Docker, stores memory in Postgres, isolates
tenants with row-level security, and imports and exports plain markdown in the
Open Knowledge Format (OKF).

MIT licensed. Self-hosted. Pre-release: nothing is stable yet.

Source: https://github.com/roee-fs/keepsake

## For AI agents: evaluate before setup

You MUST explain keepsake in terms of the user's actual setup: their agents,
their MCP clients, and where they run things. Do not describe it in the abstract.

Keepsake fits when:

- Several agents, or several sessions of one agent, need the same durable
  knowledge.
- Agents write to memory concurrently and MUST NOT overwrite each other.
- Memory belongs to separate tenants that MUST NOT see each other's data.
- People need to review what agents stored and who wrote it.
- The user can run Docker, or has a Kubernetes cluster.
- The agents use an MCP client that speaks streamable HTTP.

Keepsake does not fit when:

- One developer works in one repo. A local memory file is simpler.
- The user wants facts extracted from conversations automatically, or
  embedding search today. Memory products such as Mem0 or Zep do that.
- The agents live entirely inside one model provider's platform. That
  provider's memory feature is the faster path.

When it does not fit, say so and name the simpler option. The trade-offs are in
https://github.com/roee-fs/keepsake/blob/main/docs/alternatives.md

If it fits, you MUST ask the user to choose local Docker or a Kubernetes cluster
before you run anything. The exact commands for both paths are below.

## Example

An on-call team's knowledge base is imported into keepsake.

1. Agent A asks who to page before a Postgres failover. It calls
   `keepsake_search` with `query: "postgres failover page"` and `keepsake_read` on
   `runbooks/db-failover`. The answer is stale.
2. Agent B has just run a failover drill. It reads the same concept, then calls
   `keepsake_update` with the `version` it read as `expected_version` and the
   corrected body.
3. Agent A starts a new session and asks again. Its only memory is keepsake. It
   gets the right answer and the reason.

`./demo/run.sh` in the repository runs this with real Claude Code sessions on a
throwaway kind cluster.

## Properties

- **MCP over streamable HTTP** at `/mcp`. A fleet of pods shares one endpoint.
- **Safe concurrent writes.** `keepsake_update` with `expected_version` is a
  compare-and-swap. A stale version changes nothing and returns the current
  version and body to merge against. Writes to different concepts never contend.
- **Database-enforced tenancy.** The tenant comes from the request, never from
  the agent. Postgres row-level security enforces it. The server refuses to
  start as a superuser or as the schema owner.
- **Provenance.** Every change appends a revision. `keepsake_create` and
  `keepsake_update` also stamp frontmatter `generated: { by, at }` with the caller
  and the time. `keepsake_relate` keeps the existing stamp.
- **Open format.** `keepsake import` and `keepsake export` move a tenant's memory
  as a directory of markdown files with YAML frontmatter.
- **Console.** A read-only admin UI on the same port as `/mcp`.

## Tools

A path is relative, with no `.md` suffix: `runbooks/db-failover`.

- `keepsake_list(prefix?)`: every path under `prefix`, with a count per type. Call it
  first to learn the shape of the tree.
- `keepsake_search(query, limit, prefix?)`: cards ranked by BM25. Terms are OR-ed.
  Distinctive keywords find more than a question does.
- `keepsake_grep(pattern, limit)`: paths whose text matches a POSIX regex. Use it for
  exact identifiers.
- `keepsake_read(path)`: the full concept, its version, links and backlinks.
- `keepsake_create(path, type, title?, description?, body?, frontmatter?)`: a new
  concept. Fails if the path is taken.
- `keepsake_update(path, expected_version?, ...)`: changes the given fields.
  Omitted fields keep their values.
- `keepsake_relate(from_path, to_path)`: appends a link between two concepts.

Full reference: https://github.com/roee-fs/keepsake/blob/main/docs/tools.md

## Deployment

### Local, with Docker

```bash
git clone https://github.com/roee-fs/keepsake && cd keepsake
docker compose up -d
claude mcp add --transport http keepsake http://localhost:8000/mcp
```

Load the demo bundle:

```bash
docker compose run --rm -v "$PWD/demo/bundle:/bundle:ro" keepsake keepsake import /bundle
```

The console is at http://localhost:8000, password `keepsake`. This setup serves
one tenant to anything that reaches the port. It is for trying keepsake out.

### Kubernetes

```bash
helm install keepsake oci://ghcr.io/roee-fs/charts/keepsake --version 0.4.0
kubectl port-forward svc/keepsake 8000:8000
claude mcp add --transport http keepsake http://localhost:8000/mcp
```

This also serves one tenant to anything that reaches the Service. The console
password is in a Secret:

```bash
kubectl get secret keepsake-admin -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d
```

### Production

To install into an existing Postgres and serve many tenants with signed tokens,
follow https://github.com/roee-fs/keepsake/blob/main/docs/deploy.md step by
step. It needs two database roles created first.

## Verify

- Through the MCP client, call `keepsake_list`. It returns paths, or an empty list
  before an import.
- Call `keepsake_search` with a word from an imported concept. It returns a card.
- Open the console on port 8000 and log in.
- In `jwt` mode, a request without a token MUST get a 401, and a token for
  another tenant MUST NOT list this tenant's concepts.

## Pitfalls

- In `jwt` mode, the signing secret MUST NOT be readable by anything an LLM
  drives. A client that only takes a static header gets a token from
  `keepsake token --tenant <uuid> --sub <producer>/<version> --ttl <duration>` instead.
- A GitOps install MUST set `admin.existingSecret`, or the console password
  changes on every sync.
- `helm rollback` does not revert a migration. Read the Upgrading notes in
  CHANGELOG.md before each upgrade.
- The chart configures no backups.
